posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Oaktree:

Another game in.  Drawn-out affair between Apostate and Visionary, Legacy, and Parse.  Once again in the Pike Industrial Complex.A recurring issue with some 3-hero groups is too much support and sometimes a lack of damage capacity when you need it.  That's when you end up depending on those one-shot damage cards of Visionary and Legacy for some extra pop at the right time.  And Parse's ability to make damage irreducible is quite useful against relics when they pile up and protect each other.Apostate was eventually flipped and holding out fairly well.  However, Legacy was established and was intercepting damage and using Next Evolution to avoid damage and keep the heroes in the game.At this point the environment took an active part.  A pack of mutated lab rats put in an appearance.  In one round they chewed Visionary into incapacitation.  In the next round they got an additional damage bonus and proceeded to chew up relics and demons.  Which left Apostate vulnerable to Legacy and Parse to finish him off.

Man, you need to stop taking three epic supports in the same game.

Throw a EOW Bunker or Expat or a alternate wraith in there, if you are rocking some top support throw in some lesser played damage.  We don't want to be stuck playing really crappy teams at the end of this.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
My good friends from Portland came East Coast side and we got in a very good game vs Voss. Young Legacy (new player), DWFixer (new player), Redeemer Fanatic and Setback (me).

Things looked really bad early. Both starships showed up within the first 3 rounds and they bashed on us good. Everyone was around 10-14 HP by the time we got Voss to flip still at full health. But we pulled out a win just as Voss played his first Forced Deployment. It was a nailbitter, but Wrathful Retribution and Wrong Time and Place at the 11th hour changed everything. I love when games turn out this way, especially when playing with new people. They are always very memorable just because of how bad it looked early on. 

Setback has been growing so fast on me since release. So much fun. And everytime I'd Risk a "Whoops, Sorry!" it would draw some good laughs from the new players who really got into the thematics of it all.

Expatriette, Haka, and Mr. Fixer vs. advanced Dreamer in the Realm of Discord.  Game ended with Expatriette at 1, Haka at 6 (solely from a last-round 4-point Haka of Restoration just in case), and Fixer at 2.  Luckily timed Grease Guns and a Ground Pound, and some help from the environment reducing villain damage or providing additional hero targets via Imbued Vitality were the only things to keep the heroes alive.  I admit that I cheesed it by using Savage Mana to destroy a bunch of projections right after she flipped, but Expatriette having nothing but ammo, Reloads, and an SMG for the first three turns makes me feel less bad about it.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Nightmist, The Sentinels, and Fanatic just took on The Chairman in The Block.

Nightmist did an Oblivion on the first few underboss-thugs to show up, and The Sentinels weathered the all-hero damage pretty well.  After that Nightmist went into Mist Form while high HP hero and tanked retaliation damage from the Operative while Fanatic and The Sentinels kept pace with the underbosses and thugs.

Things got a little wild with the appearance of a Prison Break - which put all five underbosses into play by the end of the villain turn.  Fanatic countered with an End of Days, but that pulled Nightmist out of Mist Form and cleaned out whatever ongoings the heroes had, such as Sentinel Tactics.

With a short villain deck the heroes and The Chairman flipped the heroes changed tactics.  Nightmist Mistbound the villain deck once, and beyond that an Enboldened Writhe was checking the bottom of the villain deck every turn for the other Prison Break.  It was eventually found and discarded.

The environment had been relatively benign so far, but now had two Time-Crazed Prisoners in play and a 9-card trash pile.  They proceeded to obliterate the Operative's hit points over the next two rounds.  Nightmist went back into Mist Form right before they finished with the Operative and started on her.  The Environment then cleaned itself up with a Lock Down on the last card in its deck.

The heroes started on The Chairman himself with a vengeance after finishing off the crippled Operative.  A turn later Fanatic drew Wrathful Retribution and finished The Chairman off the round afterwards.

A solid team effort where each hero pulled their weight and made an important contribution to the victory.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Gloomweaver taken down in Insula Primalis by a support team; DW Nightmist, Argent Adept, and Omnitron-X

Hero team weakness early on was simply inflicting damage.  Nightmist handled the initial set of zombies, but after that Voodoo Pins accumulated on her and she soon couldn't keep a hand in play.  Heroes did a lot of healing as Gloomy's cultists and some zombies did limited damage - mainly due to OX having high HP and the right plating in play. 

Argent Adept built up songs and instruments and OX accumulated a component set.  Sarabande of Destruction kept the dinosaurs in check and OX was keeping the zombies in check.

The game turned once OX got a Defensive Blast card in play.  With a +1 damage bonus from the Adept OX played Flechettes and triggered a defensive blast that swept out the voodoo pins, cultists, and zombies that were active.  This allowed Nightmist to get back into action.  From there Gloomy's relics were rapidly trashed; either immediately by Argent Adept after coming into play, or detected by Nightmist on the top of Gloomy's deck and then TImeshifted to the trash by OX.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Standard quick fight involving Plague Rat vs. Bunker, Scholar, and Eternal Haka at Freedom Tower.

All the heroes infected early on - and two of them took the damage to remove Infected once Plague Rat flipped.  Scholar played support, tanked a bit, and generally just held on.  Bunker got Flak Gun, Omni-cannon, and Grenade Launcher out and then sat there in Turret Mode and pounded away.  Haka mainly used Taiha, but also played Ground Pound twice in order to reduce the damage taken somewhat.  Also noted that Punish The Weak is not that bad a card for Haka in this situation since it reduces damage being inflicted on other heroes while infected.

Heroes were down to 5-8 HP each when Plague Rat went down.  Lots of ongoings into play and the heroes were all infected again by then as well.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Scholar, Nightmist, and Parse vs Citizen Dawn on a Mobile Defense Platform.

Scholar played tank for most of the game with a Iron Form that shrugged off minor attacks thoughout the game.  He did Truth Seeker and other attacks as opportunity permitted amidst plays to keep his hand size built up.  MDF supplying a large quantity of harmless targets helped him out as well.  His team support cards mixed well with the other heroes, especially allowing Nightmist extra plays to get equipment out or cast additional spells.

Nightmist rolled out Master of Magic and the Necklace and then started casting Oblivion repeatedly to pound on non-hero targets.  Lost everything to THAT CARD, built it up again, did a Mist Fueled Recovery to get HP back up, and then back to Oblivion or Planar Banishment when Dawn started rolling out ongoings.  The Amulet was out by then as well and Dawn caught quite a bit of redirected damage.

Parse did a mixed support role.  She discovered early that a Aurora was on the bottom of Dawn's deck (and it was left there).  The other Aurora wiped out her Critical Multiplier cards.  Targetting Arrow on Dawn helped quite a bit in the late game running down of Dawn's HP - especially since Nightmist was using Elder Ring to boost damage even further. 

And I'd argue that Dawn's citizens helped the hero cause.  Initial citizens where Truth and Spring.  Initial villain card play was Dare blowing Truth away.  And the ongoing for bringing citizens back from the trash never made it into play.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Cosmic Omnitron attacks Freedom Tower, and is opposed by Dark Visionary, Golem Unity, and EOW Bunker.

The Giant Robot is essentially owned by Visionary while Unity arranges for a bot posse to tear up any drones that appear.  Bunker did a good tank role by playing Heavy Plating and using the Repair Module to heal up and stay high HP. 

Visionary buried Omnitron's "good" cards with Turmoil, and had Wrest The Mind cards available for dealing with both of Omnitron's EPEs and using them to wreck havoc on Omnitron itself.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Spite (Agent of Gloom) vs Eternal Haka, Omnitron-X, and The Scholar in The Final Wasteland

Game starts in Spiite's favor as he gets three drugs flipped before enough victims are in the Safe House to flip him.  And then he knocks the heroes around a bit more before they empty the Safe House back out.  Omnitron-X has some components out and thus is playing an extra on-going every turn for one drug to put back in his hand.  Haka is doing some damage, but taking punishment.  The Scholar is tanking, and helping out with some support cards.  But the tide seems to be running against the heroes and OX is about to go down.

And Spite simply got crushed after that point.

Between Scholar playing a card that stopped Spite from causing damage for a turn and Haka playing Ground Pound Spite spent four turns not touching the heroes.  He also was pretty inefficient at taking out victims since Potential Sidekick sat out there and gave the heroes extra cards repeatedly.  In that calm OX assembled a full component set and just chipped away at Spite while providing healing.  Haka played Haka of Battle to boost Taiha damage three times.  And Scholar eventually discarded a 19-card hand to set Spite up for the killing blow by Haka.

(Aside: Looking at the drugs in play I also think I could have kept Scholar in play indefinitely.  Two Flesh To Iron would soak Spite's attacks and he'd need an extra ongoing in play each turn for a drug to push back to his hand.  Incap plays from OX and Haka get him a draw and a card play to put the extra ongoing back out.  With Scholar's draw that would give him enough cards for the discards to keep both Flesh To Iron cards out.  Not a lot of extra space to kill Spite, but I think he'd eventually win out - especially with a card like Potential Sidekick out there helping him with additional card draws to help power an attack or build a LEE engine.)

The environment played one vat explosion early, and from there mainly tossed out Mutant Lab Rats.   Soon afterwards Wraith played multiple copies of Mega Computer and neutered that as a threat as well.

Played 3 games tonight.

Game 1:  Apostate in Rook City vs. DW Mr. Fixer, Parse, KNYFE, and Setback    -   Hero victory.  Apostate didn't stand a chance.  Only two relics came into play (Pendant and Orb of Delusions).  The rest was one Apocalypse on round 3, a few direct damages and some Fiendish Pugilists.  Special Recognition goes out to Tony Taurus for helping avoid an Apocalypse and some "play the next villain card" cards.

posts.name: Theta_Sigma
posts.cooked:
It was a close match, but eventually Chrono-Ranger, Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Omnitron-X and Absolute Zero were able to defeat La Capitan.

 

And by close, I mean everyone was below 5 health at the end.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
La Capitan appears at the Pike Industrial Complex and is opposed by Golem Unity, Freedom Tempest, and Omnitron-X.

Crew pours out quickly as the heroes can't take the ship down quickly.  Battleforged adds to this by thumping lab rats in order to get more villain cards into play.  On the fllp-side some early bot plays by Unity (Champion Bot, Swift Bot, Turret Bot) take up damage otherwise aimed at heroes. 

Unity gets more bots out using Construction Pylons and the Modular Workshop, and Bee Bots prove vital in that they prevented extensive hero damage from two of the three vat explosions that occurred.  Bee Bots also took out villain ongoing cards a few times as well.  A few Platform Bots, Cyro Bot, and a Raptor Bot also turned up.

Tempest played an early Electrical Storm, but later had it stolen.  He also got Grevious Hailstorm and Cleansing Rain into use as well, plus his usual blasting one-shots.  He also used his default power to destroy cards sitting under La Capitan after she flipped.

Omnitron-X helped out with extra card plays for himself and the other heroes.  He also got the Ablative Plating out early and tanked a lot of shots from La Capitan and Trueshot as a result.  A few Defensive Blasts were triggered, and he also managed to build up a good component stack.

La Capitan flipped once with four cards beneath her, and immediately added three more via a Temporal Thief play.  However, she was flipped back two turns later and wasn't able to keep any crew active for more than two turns.  Damage coming at her from all three heroes, plus vats inflicting damage as well.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Bomber Blade attacks Legacy, Absolute Zero, and DW Expatriette in The Final Wasteland.

Blade rolls out on-goings and one shots instead of targets to charge his bombs.  By the time he does the heroes flip him.  On his flipped side his gets flabbergasted after he death rays Expatriette twice for no apparent effect (Thank you Flak Jacket twice over).

Legacy rolled out Inspiring Presence, Motivational Charge, and the Legacy Ring, after which he played a one-shot now and then and otherwise Galvanized and pummeled Baron Blade for extra damage.  He also had Danger Sense in play and soaked environment attacks multiple times.

Absolute Zero rolled out his modules in the first two turns and then used one shots and base power to alternately blast Baron Blade and heal.  He also got a very useful one shot in that stripped Baron Blade of Living Forcefield and Backlash Field.

DW Expatriette started the game with Tactical Shotgun in hand.  She used that until it was lost when Baron Blade flipped.  Added a Flak Jacket and also used Shock Rounds with it.  With the damage bonus Legacy was supplying she simply blasted Blade's HP down.  After Blade flipped she played an Assault Rifle and pinged away at Blade and the Wasteland monsters that had turned up.  When she lost the first Flak Jacket to Blade's attack she played a second one that was in hand.

The Wasteland Monsters were not that dangerous to the heroes. Legacy's Danger Sense avoided damage, Baron Blade was low or 2nd low HP multiple times, and the Snowman was attacking AZ without any net effect.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Slugfest in Freedom Tower;  Ermine, Friction, and Proleteriat vs. Rook City Wraith, Naturalist, and Haka.

Heroes concentrated on taking a single villain down at a time - Friction first, then Ermine, and then Proleteriat last.  Which generally worked out since when each went down they took the largest villain stack of ongoings and nemesis cards currently deployed each time.  And Proleteriat never unleashed his mass damage card.

Wraith mainly used targetted Throwing Knives and eventually shifted to Razor Ordnance with the Utility Belt eventually coming out and making the reduction of Proleteriat's clone force much easier.  Naturalist started in Crocodile form, and then shifted to Rhino to help tank damage.  Haka just beat on things and never managed to get a Rampage card.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
A near run in a contest I'd normally consider to generate a blowout.

Ambuscade in Insula Primalis vs. Mr Fixer, Expatriette, and Freedom Wraith.

Ambuscade starts with 2 Reactive Platings in play.  Cloaking Device came out by Round 3, and came out of the trash twice as well.  He stayed hidden and chipped away at the heroes while letting the dinos do the dirtly work of wearing the heroes down.  Then he started rolling out devices and pounding away directly.  Plus a late play of Charged Attacks - which actually proved to be his undoing.

The environment played a part from the beginning.  Enraged T-Rex in the first round, and the second T-Rex came out in Round 4.  Raptors, poisonous plant life, and the Volcano as well.  Constant damage to the heroes, as well as a distraction from trying to hurt Ambuscade's devices or him when the cloak was down. And Obsidian Fields building up and making cards like Driving Mantis useless.

Fixer was... Fixer.  Dual Crowbars and a style depending on what needed hammered on.  Some vital card plays as well.  Grease Gun, Salvage Yard, and Grease Gun again late to get the heroes a touch of breathing room.  Expatriette rolled out guns, some ammo, and just blasted away constantly - mainly with the Assault Rifle.  Unload got played and resulted in the use in a single turn of Pride, Assault Rifle, and Tactical Shotgun in order to sweep out some dinos and also take down three devices.  RPG never turned up, which would have been useful.

Wraith had what I consider an off game.  Just couldn't get equipment out that quickly or use it that effectively.  Base power (hit two targets for 1 melee) was used a lot more than I expected to.  Grappling Hook only came up once, no Impromptu Invention cards, no Throwing Knives, just mixes of her non-weapon and support equipment.

Last round came around with each hero at less than 4 HP (1, 2, and 4).  Ambuscade has about 20 HP left, Charged Attacks, and two Automated Turrets in play.  Two Obsidian Fields are adding to the fun.  Fixer does a few damage to Ambuscade and one of the turrets.  Expatriette plays Hollow points, and uses the Shotgun on Ambuscade since using the Assault Rifle would kill a Turret and trigger Charged Attacks to kill all three heroes.  Things are pretty grim. 

Wraith plays Inventory Barrage and blows up five pieces of equipment to take out most of Ambuscade's remaining points.  Base power hits Ambuscade for 3 points, and the second attack kills a damaged turret - which triggers Charged Attacks and is used to take out Ambuscade (and win the game).

I didn't know you had villains you didn't play against. The games aren't fun? Not even with the Cursed Acolyte?

Even the Cursed Acolyte couldn't save the punching bag that is GloomWeaver. Which is why I am not a fan of playing against GloomWeaver, I have only lost once out of I can't even remember how many games, with the main reason I lost being an environment kept screwing the heroes quite a bit and the Relics and Cursed Acolytes would not stay dead. Luckily, Skinwalker does a nice job patching it up, so I am willing to play him.

Spite, it's just a game where you wait for Spite to flip, unless you have a way to lower his damage output. Then post flip, he does the samething he does every game, even making the environment do almost nothing, unless what came out does something upon entering play or end of turn. The most problematic games against Spite are the ones where he takes forever to flip. Best strategy to beating Spite is building up and not laying a finger on him. Like GloomWeaver, the promo actually allowed to use his deck again!

Miss Information is a lot like Spite, but much worse. You go through a big portion of the game without anything to hit, your cards in play are constantly destroyed, and you discard from hand a lot as well. Her difficulty comes from the length of time it takes her to flip, which I don't find fun. Two things you do before her flip, draw tons of cards or play enough cards to outpace her destruction.

Basically, yeah I don't find these villains very fun to play against. But I was a playtester on all these, so I blame myself partially for how they turned out. Such as actually enjoying games against Spite early on, until the realization that Spite makes all games the same. Not being vocal enough about how I actually enjoyed GloomWeaver before the nerfing. And not actually playtesting at all when it was Miss Information's turn.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Randomly rolled Sentinels and Visionary against randomly rolled the Chairman and Silver Gulch; Legacy was picked deliberately because I absolutely refuse to play against the Chairman unless Legacy is involved. The Chairman’s first cards were Rook City Is Mine! and the Broker, which put a copy of Sustain the Portal and Sheriff Pratt into play. It wasn’t the worst possible set-up.

I wasn’t willing to play the top card of the villain deck just yet, so I didn’t play a card with Legacy and just Galvanized everyone. The Sentinels came up next and played Horrifying Dichotomy, prompting the Chairman to get a useless copy of Perfect Human Specimens before the Sentinels destroyed the Informant and got in four points of damage to the Operative, prompting Legacy to take a single point of retaliatory damage. Mainstay buffed the Sentinels, then Visionary, who had no useful cards, put out a copy of Psychic Maelstrom to beat down the Broker enough for Sheriff Pratt to almost definitely target and kill her during the environment phase and to hit the Operative for three more points. She used Enlighten on Legacy to try to get a copy of Lead From the Front out, since he already had Next Evolution and the Legacy Ring in his hand, but no luck.

A copy of Explosives Wagon came out on the environment phase; I groaned a little in anticipation of suckage to come but took consolation in watching Pratt kill the Broker for me. Legacy took two points of spiteful revenge. Another copy of Rook City Is Mine! came out, bringing out a Water Trough and Cyrus Hayes. The Muscle and the Enforcers followed, which I thought was pretty lucky, though it kind of broke my heart to discard Aura of Vision to keep the Idealist from taking 4 HP of damage from the Enforcers.

I weighed my options carefully and decided the best long-term strategy for survival was to play Next Evolution and immunize Legacy to melee damage, since Explosives Wagon was basically Galvanizing everyone for free anyway. The Sentinels played Unique Capabilities because I was pretty sure they were going to play Dark Delusions anyway, but it never hurts to have two extra cards in your hand before committing to that. I pinged the Underboss and the Thug so Cyrus and Pratt could do the wetwork for me, and hit the Operative for another 4 HP before buffing their armor again. Visionary had nothing useful to do again, so she tossed out a Mental Divergence just in case we needed an card to sacrifice to a Thief later and again failed to give Legacy a Lead From the Front.

I don’t honestly remember the next several turns in that kind of detail, and you probably don’t need the specifics anyway. Gunmen and Cover came out in roughly equal proportion, so they were effectively immune to all but the most concentrated attempts at damaging them and finished off the villain targets I’d softened up; Legacy got out his ring and his Motivational Charge so the heroes were only losing a little HP very slowly while he was more or less immunizing the team to the Operative’s counterattacks (I never did draw Danger Sense, go figure); the Sentinels were my primary damage-dealers, carefully wearing the villain targets for the environment targets while maintaining armor at all times; Visionary didn’t get many useful cards and did whatever seemed least stupid at the moment, mostly manipulating the environment and always trying to get Legacy the life-saving Lead From the Front. It didn’t come out until the neighborhood of round 8. By the time it came out, everyone’s HP was low enough that Writhe with his Caliginous Form was doing most of the party-shielding anyway. Visionary started getting Suggestion cards around round 6 I carefully stockpiled for later.

With the help from all the cowboys, I actually flipped the Chairman at the beginning of round four. The environment cards couldn’t help me against him, so the heroes focused carefully on him while still trying to leave henchmen for the environment to handle.

Probably my favorite moment in the game was round five, when Tyler Hayes was going to kill off the Explosives Wagon and I very cynically manipulated the damage distribution to be wipe out as many henchmen as possible, then attack the wagon to blow it up so the other cover cards would immunize the rest of my teams of gunslingers from the damage, and only after the damage buff was gone did I allow him to hit the heroes. They were limping along after that, but a steady stream of HP from Legacy and the Sentinels kept them limping rather than falling over while Decoy Projections kept Visionary alive a lot longer than she deserved to live and kept the Contract buried under the essentially useless Enforcers. He did come out eventually, but Visionary managed to keep the deck from shuffling with all those stockpiled Suggestion cards until after the Operative died.

I was on my game, but I don’t delude myself: it was at least fifty percent luck I won. Extremely lucky early draws from each and every deck and some very well-timed cards later in the game meant only the Idealist died from a bad combination of Tyler Hayes and the other Sustain the Portal (while Caliginous Form kept up a steady stream of ping-damage on the Chairman that would make him retaliate against his own henchmen and kill them, which I will never stop thinking is funny), but in the final round, with the Chairman at 1 HP, the Sentinels played Second Chance just to get her back…so she could zap him and end the game.

Dark Watch Mr. Fixer, Ra, and Golem Unity just pretty much mudstomped Baron Blade in the Mobile Defense Platform. I feel kind of bad about how easy it went. Mr. Fixer had a Pipe Wrench and a Jack Handle in his hand in the first draw, Ra got out his stick and his Flame Barrier, and Golem Unity was able to get out garbage cards to sacrifice to Mr. Fixer while Bee Bots blew up Baron Blade’s Backlash Fields;* but since Ra was counterattacking Blade’s counterattacks, I was actually kind of glad the Backlash Fields stayed in place as long as they did. Mr. Fixer was the damage magnet with his Pipe Wrench to keep him from getting hit too hard. All was said and done in fourteen rounds, though a big part of that was Blade never finding a Devious Disruption, an Elemental Redistributor, or a Slash and Burn. Everyone was at either 6 or 7 HP when the battle ended.

*EDIT: Say “Bee Bots blew up Baron Blade’s Backlash Fields” five times fast.
